items.html: Thus it is found that these two — Tzitz and Tzitzit — are so called after the verse "And he took me by the lock of my head," which are the aspect of the hairs. Also, the matter of Tzitzit is an expression of gazing (histaklut), as above. And the reason is that these hairs, which are in the locks of hair of Arich Anpin or of Zeir Anpin, were drawn and hanging in order to receive the faces of Arich Anpin and Zeir Anpin, and they covered their eyes, so that neither would Arich Anpin gaze upon Zeir Anpin, nor Zeir Anpin upon his Nukva, to shine one into the other. And through our deeds in the commandment of Tzitzit, we cast and throw those hairs behind Arich Anpin and Zeir Anpin, so that Arich Anpin might gaze upon Zeir Anpin, and Zeir Anpin upon his Nukva.
